questions.q: What is different about this bug compared to the one in Lessons 11-13?
options: It never throws an error anywhere in the pipeline; the data is simply wrong while everything reports success
It causes the nightly load to fail every single night
It only affects the Spectrum query path, never Redshift
It is caused by the exact same IAM permissions gap as before
questions.explain: The ETL job, the COPY, and the schedule all complete successfully — there's no error anywhere, which is the lesson's core point.

questions.q: What does comparing the Finance report before vs. on/after 2026-09-15 reveal?
options: A sharp boundary at that date: clean region values before it, garbled date-shaped region values and near-zero totals after it
No difference at all between the two date ranges
Revenue is actually higher after the cutover with no anomalies
The region column is completely empty in both periods
questions.explain: The symptom has a sharp boundary at the cutover date rather than a gradual drift, pointing to something that changed on that exact date.

questions.q: What do the raw CSV headers from before and after the cutover show?
options: A new sales_channel column was inserted in the middle of the row, right after order_date, shifting every later column's position
The files are byte-for-byte identical before and after the cutover
A column was removed from the row, not added
The column order was alphabetized starting on the cutover date
questions.explain: after.csv's header has sales_channel inserted between order_date and region, which before.csv does not have.

questions.q: Why did northfield-raw-crawler misread the schema change?
options: It's on-demand only and was manually re-run after the layout changed, sampling a mix of old- and new-layout files and mapping columns positionally instead of by name for the shifted files
It runs automatically every night as part of the Lesson 8 schedule and always reads correctly
It was never run again after the initial setup in earlier lessons
AWS Glue crawlers are incapable of ever misreading a CSV schema
questions.explain: The crawler is on-demand, not scheduled, and a later manual run across mixed-layout files caused it to misread the new column's position.

questions.q: What has this lesson confirmed, and what hasn't happened yet?
options: The exact cause, cutover date, and mechanism are confirmed; the fix and backfill haven't been applied yet — that's Lesson 15
The bug has already been fully fixed by the end of this lesson
The cause is still unknown at the end of this lesson
The backfill of corrected data has already been completed
questions.explain: This lesson is the diagnosis half only, matching the same reproduce-before-fixing discipline used in Lessons 11-12.
